Private Worship
PRY-vit WUR-ship
n.
“Private” from Latin privatus, “set apart, belonging to oneself”; “worship” from Old English weorþscipe. The individual believer’s personal worship of God.

📖 Biblical Definition

Private worship is the personal, individual worship of God by the believer alone—the whole of his secret devotion, comprising private prayer, the reading and meditation of Scripture, praise, self-examination, and communion with God in the closet. It is the third sphere of worship, alongside public worship (the church assembled) and family worship (the household), and it is the most hidden and personal of the three. Its charter is Christ’s instruction to enter into the closet, shut the door, and pray to the Father in secret, who sees in secret and rewards openly. Private worship embraces all the elements of devotion exercised by the individual alone with God: secret prayer, in which the soul pours out its confessions, petitions, intercessions, and thanksgivings; the private reading and meditation of the Word, in which God speaks to the soul and the soul ponders His truth; private praise and the singing of psalms; self-examination, in which the heart is searched before God; and the cultivation of communion with God, the soul’s intimate fellowship with its Lord. Private worship holds a peculiar importance as the truest barometer of the spiritual life, for it is exercised with no witness but God, and a man is in religion what he is in secret and no more. Public and family worship may be sustained by habit, duty, or the eyes of others; private worship, hidden from all human view, reveals the real state of the soul. It is the hidden root from which the visible branches of family and public devotion draw their life: a soul vigorous in private worship will flourish in the assembly, while a soul that has deserted its closet will wither, however diligent its outward religion. The believer is therefore to maintain a faithful, regular life of private worship—a set time and place to meet God alone, day by day—giving himself to secret prayer, the Word, meditation, and communion with his Lord. Its neglect is the slow starvation of the soul; its faithful practice is the secret of all vital and growing godliness, the place where the deepest dealings between God and the soul are transacted, and the hidden spring of a fruitful Christian life.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828, under WORSHIP, distinguishes private worship—that performed by an individual in secret—from public and family worship.

expand to see more

PRIVATE, a. — ...2. Peculiar to one’s self; belonging to or concerning an individual only; as private opinion; private devotion. Private worship, the worship of God performed by an individual in secret or retirement.

WORSHIP, n. — ...the homage paid to God; when offered by an individual alone, it is private worship.

📖 Key Scripture

Matthew 6:6 — "But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly."

Psalm 5:3 — "My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up."

Psalm 63:6 — "When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches."

Daniel 6:10 — "...he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

No major postmodern redefinition, but private worship is widely neglected—the closet deserted, personal devotion abandoned amid distraction and busyness—hollowing out the spiritual life from its hidden root.

expand to see more

Private worship is corrupted chiefly by neglect—the desertion of the closet that quietly hollows out the whole spiritual life from its hidden root. In an age of ceaseless distraction, perpetual busyness, and the unending demands of screens and devices, the believer’s private devotion is among the first casualties: the set time of secret prayer and the Word is crowded out, deferred, and finally abandoned, until the soul lives without any regular, personal meeting with God alone. A man may maintain his public worship and even his family devotions while his private worship has long since collapsed—and such a soul, whatever its outward appearance, is withering, for private worship is the hidden spring from which the visible branches draw their life. Its neglect is the slow starvation of the soul, often unnoticed until the inward decay shows itself in the outward life.

The recovery of private worship is the recovery of vital, growing godliness at its source. Because it is exercised with no witness but God, private worship is the truest measure of the spiritual life: a man is in religion what he is in his closet and no more. The believer is to maintain a faithful, regular life of private worship—a set time and place to meet God alone, day by day—giving himself to secret prayer, the reading and meditation of the Word, private praise, self-examination, and communion with his Lord. This hidden discipline, faithfully kept, is the secret of all flourishing religion: it feeds the soul, deepens communion with God, fortifies against temptation, and supplies the inward vigor that makes family and public worship come alive. Tend the closet, and the whole life flourishes; desert it, and no outward devotion can long disguise the inward decay. The believer who would grow in grace and walk closely with God must, above all, be faithful in the hidden worship of his secret place, where the deepest dealings between God and the soul are transacted.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The doctrine rests on Christ’s call to worship in the closet (tameion) to the Father in secret—the soul alone seeking God in prayer, the Word, and meditation.
